newsitem.title: UK: Merrill cuts Brit Steel forecast due to stg.
newsitem.headline: Merrill cuts Brit Steel forecast due to stg.

text.p: Merrill Lynch said on Thursday it had decided to more than halve its profit forecast for British Steel Plc for the year to March 1998 because of the severe impact of sterling strength on exports.
Merrill analyst Paul Compton said the pretax profit downgrade on Wednesday to 280 million stg from 650 million for the year to March 1998 was purely due to the potential impact of the UK currency.
British Steel dipped 1-3/4 pence to 152-1/4 pence on Thursday after slipping back in late trade on Wednesday.

Merrill has retained its neutral stance on the stock. It said this year's profits would be cushioned from sterling's relentless rise by a forward-cover measure taken by British Steel which protects against currency movements in the six months ahead.
British Steel was not immediately available for comment.

Other British exporters are feeling the pain of the strong pound. After benefiting from the effective devaluation in the wake of the ERM exit four and a half years ago, UK firms now fear being priced out of some markets.
The Confederation of British Industry's December survey showed the number of UK manufacturers reporting a fall in export orders was 15 percentage points higher than those who reported a rise.
